title.narrative: Strengthening the Provision of Lifesaving CCCM Activities for Drought-Affected IDPs in Deynille District through Multisectoral Coordination in Catchment Area-Level Operations.

description.narrative:
ltp style="" class=""gtThe project intends to contribute to scaling up Camp Coordination and Camp Management in the Deynille District through the CCCM Catchment Area-Level Operations, this will be done through Area-based site-level coordination and monitoring that is critical in creating an equitable and fast emergency response for drought-affected IDPs.lt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtThe proposed project will adopt an area-based approach that prioritizes Catchment areas 18 and 19 in the Deynille district. The primary goal of this approach is to address the unique needs and challenges faced by the communities living in these areas. By concentrating resources and interventions on these specific catchment areas, the project aims to provide coordinated and effective support to vulnerable populations.lt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtTo achieve this goal, the project will use the strengthened monitoring framework of the CCCM Cluster. Through this framework, NoFYL will undertake mapping and monitoring of services at the area level. This will enhance the gap analysis for the humanitarian response and other partners involved in the delivery of services. Data collection of new arrivals and MUAC screening/referrals via New Arrival Tracker activity will be conducted to provide site-level new arrival trends and gap analysis which is critical to the overall drought response in IDP sites leading to efficient aid and service delivery to the affected population.lt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtThe project will also prioritize community engagement and site-level complaints feedback mechanism activities. To ease this, information desks and toll-free hotlines will be set up within the IDP settlements, allowing for two-way information sharing between local authorities, humanitarian agencies, and the community. This will enhance accountability among all stakeholders while ensuring strong coordination with the support of camp management.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtThrough this project, NoFYL will continue to focus on providing access to critical information in sites receiving drought-displaced new arrivals. Additionally, site-level safety audits will be conducted to inform site improvement activities and integrated initiatives focused on protection mainstreaming. Site improvement activities will evolve to include wage-paying workdays for IDPs through cash-for-work activities, which will improve the living conditions of those affected by drought while mitigating protection issues in IDP sites.lt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gt lt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtThis grant will enable NoFYL to extend its services to 178 IDP sites found in Catchment areas 18 and 19 in the Deynille district. The project will leverage on existing coordination NoFYL is leading to ensure that necessary services are delivered to the targeted communities.lt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gt lt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtNoFYL, through the area-based approach, will manage camps in catchment areas 18 and 19. Instead of focusing solely on individual sites, NoFYL will manage the catchment areas, ensuring the efficient use of resources, improving service delivery, and promoting better coordination among humanitarian actors.lt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtNoFYL, with the support and guidance of the CCCM Cluster, will be using key site-level indicators to rotate IDP site interventions in the 178 IDP sites found in Catchment areas 18 and 19 allowing NoFYL to prioritize sites with the most pressing needs and provide them with priority attention. By measuring and tracking these indicators, NoFYL can determine if sites still require emergency CCCM operations, enabling the rotation coverage to other sites with priority needs.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtThe Area Based Approach ensures effective coordination and essential service delivery by the humanitarian actors in the catchment area to the affected communities and promotes community participation in decision-making processes. Through this, the affected communities will have a say in the management of their camps, easing effective communication and coordination among humanitarian actors. Additionally, the area-based approach will ensure the efficient use of resources, maximizing the impact of NoFYL's interventions.lt/pgtltp class="sceditor-nlf"gtltbrgtlt/pgt
